content: The following text provides a detailed and systematic description of various cetacean species, organized by their taxonomic classification. Each genus and species is listed with its common name and scientific name, along with relevant notes on their recognition or classification status. The Australian Snubfin Dolphin (Orcaella heinsohni) was discovered in 2005. Due to its recent discovery, it is not recognized by Rice or the third edition of the Mammal Species of the World (MSW3) and remains subject to taxonomic revision. The genus Orcinus includes the Killer Whale (Orcinus orca), a widely recognized and studied species. The genus Peponocephala contains the Melon-headed Whale (Peponocephala electra). The genus Pseudorca includes the False Killer Whale (Pseudorca crassidens). The genus Sotalia features the Tucuxi (Sotalia fluviatilis), though further discussion on this species can be found in its dedicated article. The genus Sousa includes: The Pacific Humpback Dolphin (Sousa chinensis), The Indian Humpback Dolphin (Sousa plumbea), The Atlantic Humpback Dolphin (Sousa teuszii). The genus Stenella comprises: The Pantropical Spotted Dolphin (Stenella attenuata), The Clymene Dolphin (Stenella clymene), The Striped Dolphin (Stenella coeruleoalba), The Atlantic Spotted Dolphin (Stenella frontalis), The Spinner Dolphin (Stenella longirostris). The genus Steno includes the Rough-toothed Dolphin (Steno bredanensis). The genus Tursiops includes: The Indian Ocean Bottlenose Dolphin (Tursiops aduncus), The Common Bottlenose Dolphin (Tursiops truncatus). Rice and MSW3 tentatively agree on this classification, but further details can be found in the species article. The genus Cephalorhynchus includes: Commerson's Dolphin (Cephalorhynchus commersonii), Chilean Dolphin (Cephalorhynchus eutropia), Heaviside's Dolphin (Cephalorhynchus heavisidii), Hector's Dolphin (Cephalorhynchus hectori). The genus Delphinus includes: The Long-beaked Common Dolphin (Delphinus capensis), The Short-beaked Common Dolphin (Delphinus delphis), The Arabian Common Dolphin (Delphinus tropicalis). Rice recognizes this as a separate species, while MSW3 does not. The genus Feresa includes the Pygmy Killer Whale (Feresa attenuata). The genus Globicephala includes: The Short-finned Pilot Whale (Globicephala macrorhynchus), The Long-finned Pilot Whale (Globicephala melas). The genus Grampus includes Risso's Dolphin (Grampus griseus). The genus Lagenodelphis includes Fraser's Dolphin (Lagenodelphis hosei). The genus Lagenorhynchus includes: The Atlantic White-sided Dolphin (Lagenorhynchus acutus), The White-beaked Dolphin (Lagenorhynchus albirostris), Peale's Dolphin (Lagenorhynchus australis), The Hourglass Dolphin (Lagenorhynchus cruciger), The Pacific White-sided Dolphin (Lagenorhynchus obliquidens), The Dusky Dolphin (Lagenorhynchus obscurus). The genus Lissodelphis includes: The Northern Right Whale Dolphin (Lissodelphis borealis), The Southern Right Whale Dolphin (Lissodelphis peronii). The genus Orcaella includes: The Irrawaddy Dolphin (Orcaella brevirostris), The Australian Snubfin Dolphin (Orcaella heinsohni), discovered in 2005 and not yet recognized by Rice or MSW3. The family Monodontidae includes: The genus Delphinapterus, which contains the Beluga (Delphinapterus leucas), The genus Monodon, which contains the Narwhal (Monodon monoceros). The family Phocoenidae (porpoises) includes: The genus Neophocaena, which contains the Finless Porpoise (Neophocaena phocaenoides), The genus Phocoena, which includes: The Spectacled Porpoise (Phocoena dioptrica), The Harbour Porpoise (Phocoena phocoena), The Vaquita (Phocoena sinus), Burmeister's Porpoise (Phocoena spinipinnis), The genus Phocoenoides, which contains Dall's Porpoise (Phocoenoides dalli). The family Physeteridae (sperm whale family) includes: The genus Physeter, which contains the Sperm Whale (Physeter catodon, synonym P. macrocephalus). The family Kogiidae (treated by MSW3 as part of Physeteridae) includes: The genus Kogia, which contains: The Pygmy Sperm Whale (Kogia breviceps), The Dwarf Sperm Whale (Kogia sima). The superfamily Platanistoidea (river dolphins) includes: The family Iniidae, with the genus Inia, which contains the Amazon River Dolphin (Inia geoffrensis), The family Lipotidae (treated by MSW3 as part of Iniidae), with the genus Lipotus, which includes the extinct Baiji (Lipotus vexillifer), The family Pontoporiidae (treated by MSW3 as part of Iniidae), with the genus Pontoporia, which contains the Franciscana (Pontoporia blainvillei), The family Platanistidae, with the genus Platanista, which includes the Ganges and Indus River Dolphin (Platanista gangetica). MSW3 treats Platanista minor as a separate species, with the common names Ganges River Dolphin and Indus River Dolphin, respectively. This detailed taxonomy provides a comprehensive overview of cetacean species, their classifications, and any relevant taxonomic considerations.
